Subject: Helios RFP: Private deployment capability / SOC2 artifacts request

Marissa,

Thanks for taking our call this morning. As discussed, Helios is evaluating vendors for an on-prem/VPC private deployment. Two asks to keep things moving: a) a focused answers pack to our questionnaire (attached short list below) and b) SOC2 or equivalent evidence that covers network segregation and operator controls (we have specific auditor questions).

Top items we need answered:
- Confirmation whether the control plane can be hosted in our VPC or must be managed by Redwood.
- Operator access model (local operators, break-glass, 2FA + KMS integrations).
- Data-at-rest and egress controls in an air-gapped/on-prem mode; we want explicit egress guarantees.
- A recommended canary rollout and rollback plan for model updates in private deployments.

If possible, please attach a short runbook or diagram we can share with our integrators. We need this by end of week to align procurement and security.

Regards,
Alicia Gomez
Director, Information Security Operations
Helios Health

From: marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Helios RFP: Private deployment capability / SOC2 artifacts request

Alicia —

Thanks, great to meet earlier. Draft answers and artifacts attached; summary below and a small proposed kickoff plan so procurement has dates. I kept the answers concise and flagged any items that require a short architecture decision call.

Quick summary answers:
- Control plane: We offer two private control plane models: 1) Customer-hosted control plane (preferred for air-gapped/on-prem) where Redwood provides the control-plane image and support contracts; or 2) Redwood-managed control plane deployed into a customer VPC under an MSA with restricted API endpoints. We recommend customer-hosted for regulated workloads.
- Operator access: Local operator accounts (RBAC) with optional break-glass escalation. We integrate with customer SAML/Okta for normal access and support tying elevated operator keys to HSM/KMS workflows. All privileged operator actions are logged and routed to your SIEM via syslog/forwarder.
- Data egress: In customer-hosted mode network policies default to deny-everything; outbound egress is configurable and can be restricted to internal mirrors only. For air-gapped installs we support zero outbound by default; metrics/telemetry can be captured to local collectors only.
- Canary rollout: We propose a three-stage canary: dev -> canary (5% traffic on dedicated pool) -> staged ramp -> full. Rollback is automated via model pin/version and we include KV-cache warmup scripts in the runbook.

I've attached: RH-SOC2-2025-summary.pdf (SOC2 scope + mapping), redwood-private-deploy-runbook-v1.3.pdf (runbook + canary steps), and a network diagram (network-segmentation-diagram.png). Also attaching a procurement-friendly redlines starter (procurement-MA-terms-draft.docx).

Next steps proposed (timeline):
- Wed 29 Jul: security + infra decision call (30m) to confirm control-plane option and egress enforcement.
- Fri 31 Jul: delivery of final evidence pack for auditors if no outstanding technical blockers.
- Following week: procurement DocuSign cadence if legal terms acceptable.

If that timeline works I'll loop in our solutions engineer for a short demo of the on-prem operator flows.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Lead — Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.ai

Marissa,

Received — thank you for the quick turnaround and the attachments. A few follow-ups from our security team after an initial pass:
1) In the SOC2 summary, can you clarify which services were in-scope and whether operator workstations were included in your SOC scoping? Our auditor specifically asked about control-plane operator hosts.
2) For the customer-hosted control plane model, can you provide a minimal set of host/VM sizing and OS hardening checklist? We need this to route to our infrastructure team.
3) The runbook references syslog forwarding but not a concrete retention policy — can you advise on recommended retention for operator audit logs (we usually consider 365 days baseline)?

Also, procurement wants to see a redline-friendly MSA with a short list of non-negotiable SLAs. Is the draft you attached safe to share with them as a starting point?

Would you and Vanessa be available for the kickoff call on Wed 29 Jul at 10:00am PT?

Thanks,
Alicia
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Alicia Gomez <ops-security@helioshealth.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: ben_carter@redwood.ai, priyom_das@redwood.ai
Date: Tue, 28 Jul 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Helios RFP: Private deployment capability / SOC2 artifacts request

Alicia —

Appreciate the detailed questions. Short answers inline below and adding a few operational artifacts for the kickoff.

1) SOC2 scope: the RH-SOC2-2025-summary.pdf indicates the control plane services (auth service, control API, operator portal) were in-scope. Operator workstations were not in-scope by default; however, we can provide a guide and attest to hardening and logging recommendations that customers adopt to satisfy auditor requests. We'll mark that explicitly in the follow-up note I bring to the call.

2) Minimal host sizing & hardening checklist: Attached is a one-page starter (host-sizing-and-hardening-cheatsheet.pdf) that lists CPU/GPU-less control-plane minima, OS baselines (RHEL 8 / Ubuntu 22.04 LTS recommended), firewall rules, and kernel parameter hardening. For an HA customer-hosted control plane (2 control-plane VMs + 1 DB replica) suggested starting footprint is 4 vCPU, 16GB RAM per control plane node, and 100GB disk for logs; DB sizing depends on retention.

3) Audit log retention: We recommend 365 days for operator audit logs as baseline, with ability to configure to 7 years for customers with specific compliance needs. The runbook contains scripts to rotate and ship logs to a local S3-compatible object store.

Attachments added for kickoff: host-sizing-and-hardening-cheatsheet.pdf, runbook-extract-canary-scripts.tar.gz (tar). For the procurement question: the docx draft is intended as a starting point — it is safe to share with procurement, but we ask that any changes to SLA scope (e.g., removing rollback obligations) be flagged for a short legal review.

I'll join Wed 29 Jul at 10:00am PT. Meeting invite forthcoming from Ben.

- Vanessa Ortiz
Director, Solutions Engineering
Redwood Inference
